messages:
anna: Quick sync — thinking about introducing a cost-aware routing layer that prefers cheaper model variants for lower customer tiers and by region. It should also have automatic fallback to higher-quality variants if we detect quality regressions. High-level idea, not details yet.

mike: +1 on the idea. Two engineering concerns: 1) model compatibility (tokenization, output format) 2) how we estimate token cost before routing. We need cheap per-request cost estimate in the routing path. :thinking:

jess: For telemetry we should emit: route_decision, estimated_token_cost, chosen_variant, quality_score, fallback_trigger, and token_counts. That lets us correlate cost savings vs quality regressions.

oliver: UX note — console needs a simple toggle per-customer and a rollout slider. Folks should be able to opt-out / pin to expensive variant. Also show expected savings and recent fallback rate in the UI.

sam: Quotas/limits angle: if we route free-tier customers to cheaper variant we should also enforce a per-customer token_budget so they can't blow past cost forecasts. If budget exceeded, either degrade to a lower-rate limit or surface upsell.

mike: Implementation sketch: routing policy lives in the control plane. At request time we compute a cheap estimate: tokens_est = ceil(prompt_len / avg_chunk) + ceil(max_output_len / avg_chunk) then cost_est = tokens_est * variant_unit_cost. If cost_est <= tier_max we pick the cheaper variant, else default. Need to cache avg_chunk per model.

anna: Example policy snippet I mocked up for discussion:```json
{
  "policy": "tier_based_variant",
  "rules": [
    {"tier": "free", "preferred": "open-medium-q4", "max_token_cost": "0.0005"},
    {"tier": "pro", "preferred": "redwood-base-q2", "max_token_cost": "0.0015"}
  ],
  "fallback": "redwood-base-q2",
  "health_check": {"quality_window": 1000, "min_quality_score": 0.84}
}
```oliver: Love the JSON. Two UX asks: a) show historical quality_score for the preferred variant in the rollout modal b) expose an override button to pin per-customer or per-route.

jess: On the quality side we need a lightweight signal for immediate feedback: use a mix of synthetic prompt set evaluations (nightly) + sampled in-prod metrics: perplexity delta proxy, rerate rejects, user-supplied flags. We shouldn't wait hours to detect regressions.

mike: For fallback behavior we can implement a fast failure detector: if fallback_count > 0.5% over last 1k requests OR average quality_score < threshold, start routing X% to fallback variant immediately and escalate to full failover after N minutes. Implement as a rolling window in the routing service.

sam: How about token cost controls enforcement? Suggest adding a per-request pre-check that returns a routing_decision with estimated_cost and a flag allow_fallback. If allow_fallback=false then we either 1) reject with 402-like (insufficient budget) or 2) route but with strict rate limit. Need product to decide.

anna: Good point — product: prefer soft-fallback (rate limit + upsell message) for free tier, hard block only if explicit budget exhausted.

oliver: For rollouts: start with a 1% canary across regions, show per-region savings and fallback rate in the rollout panel. We'll want to be able to roll back by region. Also add a quick action to "pause cost-routing" for a customer.

deploy-bot: deploy triggered: feature/route-cost-aware -> canary (1%) scheduled at 2024-07-15T18:00Z (reacts :rocket:)

mike: Action items from eng-platform: 1) RFC for control-plane policy model (mike + anna) 2) telemetry event spec (jess) 3) routing service impl plan + health-check circuit (mike + sam) 4) console UX for toggles/rollout visuals (oliver) 5) small canary run (deploy) — aim for 1% -> 10% -> 100% over two weeks.

anna: I'll draft the RFC and include the example policy. Jess, can you put together the minimal telemetry schema so we can start instrumenting? Oliver, can you mock the console panel with the sliders and savings graph? I'll coordinate rollout dates with deploy. :thumbsup:

jess: Yup, will have a telemetry PR with event names + example query snippets for dashboards by EOD tomorrow.

oliver: I'll mock a lightweight panel — focus on: savings estimate, fallback rate, per-region toggle, per-customer override. Expect Figma link in ~48h.

mike: I'll start on routing service branch and prototype the token estimator + rolling detector. Sam, can you advise on quota enforcement semantics?

sam: Yep, will write a proposal for budget semantics (soft vs hard) and example error codes.

anna: Great — thanks everyone. We'll meet next week to review the RFC and first telemetry dashboard.

(reacts: anna :eyes:, jess :white_check_mark:, oliver :sparkles:)
